decisions:
# Native annotated append publication passes scoped checks; broader parity remains RED

Initial implementation: `4a0846b60`. The follow-up streams appended labels into owner-filtered mirrors without collecting all labels or rewriting the old prefix. A typed prepared-build marker distinguishes this path from ordinary appends. Mirrors retain registered versioned annotation metadata and their primary identity in the same prepared group as the new rows. History registers only `history:density-spans:1`; file-local fact markers, counts and format auxiliary offsets are not copied from the primary. Removing an absent registered key on compensation rebuilds the target metadata trie as a stream, not a history-sized array. That rare removal is not claimed logarithmic.

The final-source acceptance lane runs complete Bun files serially with the original 180000 timeout. Native public creation denial covers 3/64/65/5000 unordered annotations. An independent old live service supplies values, successful tokens and range at 512/8192, which both reopened native durable mirrors must match; fork and compaction preserve metadata. A separate complete owner file retains the parity fixture's assertions at 3/64/65/5000, including the nontrivial prefix cut, old ROW entries/physical offsets and current origins. The inherited mixed parity file is retained unchanged and is not counted as a passing complete file.

Converted-output WeakRefs at 512/8192 observe the unchanged bound two and final zero. The entire value above nine MiB remains equal. Existing ordinary append batches stay at four MiB of encoded rows with the current-row exception; prepared annotation rows and private sorting records share the same journal. The span cache cap remains 65536 bytes and the standing span window remains 1024. Ordinary unannotated appends do not instantiate an annotation collector. The unchanged facts tests verify identical metadata writes zero commit bytes and compaction removes private sorting bytes without changing live ROW bytes.

Producer/projection/row-65/cancellation/acknowledgement faults preserve exact logical causes and restore state, including after an earlier four-MiB batch, then continue on the same primary writer. Physical write/flush failures leave the writer poisoned. The physical tests compare the failure message and subsequent poison, not the exact injected physical object. Actual mirror I/O acknowledgement faults and an independently pinned metadata-value read are not added here. Original #3919 files retain their assertions and run after the shared publication changes.

Broader parity is not green. The preserved `parity-followup.log` has seven passes and three failures: old recorder replay loses duplicate-chronology rows in its 512/8192 comparisons, while native live context range drops the summary-derived compressed span [1,2] outside the capped standing window at 8192 rows. The old live service re-derives that summary span from rows. Those executions preceded the final lint-only refactor and registered-key narrowing; they are retained as earlier-source RED, not relabeled final-source acceptance. No assertion, domain, fixture size, timeout or threshold was reduced to hide them. This prevents claiming full requested semantic closure.

Native annotated producer scratch removal and the final mirror annotation publication contract have scoped passing evidence. W26/Phase 5 remain open for the recorded parity gaps, concrete provider fallback/curatedCandidate, the unchanged public ProviderNormalizationDisk RED, explicit old/disk contracts, incremental structural ranking, pending/stale capacity and accounting, normalization/cache/tails/ranges/semantic generations, global LENS/live bytes and whole heap/cache/pin capacity. Phase 6 body/key/message/tokenizer spools and guards, Phase 8 reservations, W23/W25/cutover and cold Mistral remain separate. #3917 remains separately RED without rerun, retry or suppression. Defaults and Phase 9 old-backend lifetime are unchanged. Review skipped per Andrew 2026-10-09. No OCR, push, merge, broad cleanup or enforcement change.
